reviews.title: TLRD; Is ATX3.1, PCIe5.1, has a 12V 2x6 pin cable.
reviews.comment: Okay so I'm guessing that a lot of people did what I did. I read the online description that says ATX3.1 and PCIe 5.1 with a 12V 2x6 cable. Then when you get the thing it says 3.0, 5.0 and the older (yet the same) 12VHPWR cable on the box and you thought you get ripped off. Well I started a return, thinking maybe I got older supply, and ordered the same one from Best Buy thinking well they will give me the right one. Nope exact same box and everything. So I got online; did alot of reading and contacted Corsair and this is what I found out. After cable melting issues started cropping up the older 12VHPWR cable was slightly redesigned with shorter sense pins and longer conductor terminals, but the same cable. The way to tell is to look for the H+(older) or H++(Newer) on the side of the connector that goes into the GPU . The PSU has been rated at ATX 3.1 and PCIe5.1 prior to the new standards but the packaging was never updated to reflect that. It's all confusing and made more so by the packaging. So this cable is H++ Corsair explained the standards not being updated on the packaging. So I cancelled the return and my 5090 is running great. TLRD; ATX3.1, PCIe5.1, has a 12V 2x6 pin cable.
